source_refs.note: Book p. 222: 12.2 Limits of Important Functions, own text before 12.2.1 (substitution gives 0/0; simplify by making factors and cancelling common factors).

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Pichle hisse (12.1) mein humne limit ka matlab samjha tha, aur yeh bhi dekha tha ke aksar limit nikalna bohat aasan hai: bas \(x\) ki jagah woh number rakh do jis ki taraf \(x\) ja raha hai (approach kar raha hai). Lekin har dafa yeh itna seedha nahin hota. Kabhi kabhi number rakhne se upar bhi zero aata hai aur neeche bhi zero, yani \(\frac{0}{0}\). Yeh section, 12.2, isi mushkil ka hal sikhata hai, aur saath saath kuch bohat important limits bhi deta hai jo aage calculus (differentiation) ki buniyad banti hain.
Kitab kehti hai: agar function mein woh number substitute karne (rakhne) se jis ki taraf \(x\) approach kar raha hai, humein \(\left(\frac{0}{0}\right)\) mile, to hum limit is tarah nikalte hain:

Hum diye gaye function ko algebra ki technique se simplify karte hain: agar mumkin ho to factors (zarb ke hisse) banate hain aur numerator aur denominator ke common factors ko cancel kar dete hain. Yeh tareeqa neeche aane wali important limits mein tafseel se samjhaya gaya hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se pehle ek baat zehan mein bitha lijiye: \(\frac{0}{0}\) koi number nahin hai, aur yeh jawab bhi nahin hai. Ise indeterminate form (ghair muayyan shakal, yani aisi shakal jis se value tay nahin hoti) kehte hain.
Yeh sirf itna batata hai ke function apni mojooda shakal mein us point par seedha calculate nahin ho sakta. Limit phir bhi exist kar sakti hai, aur woh koi bhi number ho sakti hai: 4, \(-2\), \(\frac{1}{2}\), kuch bhi. Is liye pehle algebra se function ki shakal badalni hai, phir number rakhna hai.
Misaal ke taur par socho ke ek darwaza band hai (\(\frac{0}{0}\)). Iska matlab yeh nahin ke kamre mein kuch nahin; bas pehle chaabi (factorization) lagani paregi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahin, humari taraf se hai, taa ke poora tareeqa ek nazar mein samajh aa jaye. Find karna hai \(\lim_{x\to 2}\frac{x^{2}-4}{x-2}\).
Sab se pehle hum substitution try karte hain: \(x = 2\) rakhne se \(\frac{4-4}{2-2} = \frac{0}{0}\). Yani seedha jawab nahin mila, is liye factorize karte hain:
\[\dfrac{x^{2}-4}{x-2} = \dfrac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x-2}\]
\[= x + 2 \quad (x \ne 2)\]
\[\lim_{x\to 2}\dfrac{x^{2}-4}{x-2} = 2 + 2 = 4\]
Kyun: \(x^{2} - 4\) do squares ka farq hai, \(a^{2} - b^{2} = (a-b)(a+b)\). Factor banate hi woh "masla paida karne wala" factor \((x-2)\) upar aur neeche dono jagah nazar aa gaya, aur cancel ho gaya.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab sab se ahem sawal: hum \((x - 2)\) ko cancel kyun kar sakte hain, jab ke zero se divide karna mana hai?
Jawab 12.1.3 mein hai. "\(x \to 2\)" ka matlab hai ke \(x\) number 2 ke bohat bohat qareeb aata hai, jaise 1.9, 1.99, 1.999 ya 2.01, 2.001, lekin kabhi 2 ke barabar nahin hota. Is liye limit lete waqt \(x - 2\) kabhi zero nahin hota, aur use cancel karna bilkul jaiz (allowed) hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{0}{0}\) wala common factor hamesha wohi hota hai jo us point par zero ban jata hai. Agar \(x \to a\) par \(\frac{0}{0}\) aaye, to numerator aur denominator dono mein factor \((x - a)\) talaash karein.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Aage ke sub-sections mein is common factor ko hatane ke teen auzaar (tools) istemal honge:
1. Factorization, jaise \(x^{n} - a^{n} = (x-a)(\dots)\) (12.2.1 mein).
2. Rationalization (jazr wali terms ko conjugate se zarb dena), jab square roots maujood hon (12.2.2 mein).
3. Infinity par limits (\(\frac{\infty}{\infty}\) type) ke liye denominator ki sab se bari power se divide karna (12.2.3 se 12.2.5 tak).
Yani yeh chhota sa section poore 12.2 ka naqsha (map) hai. Jab bhi aage koi sawal aaye, khud se poochiye: "substitution se kya mila? Agar \(\frac{0}{0}\), to kaun sa tool lagega?"

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(\lim_{x\to 3}\frac{x^{2}-9}{x-3}\) mein substitution se kya milta hai, aur limit kya hogi?
Jawab: \(x = 3\) rakhne se \(\frac{0}{0}\). Factor: \(\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3} = x + 3\). Ab \(x = 3\) rakhein: limit \(= 6\).

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Paper mein hamesha pehle substitution dikhaiye aur likhiye "\(\frac{0}{0}\) form". Yeh ek line examiner ko batati hai ke aap factorize kyun kar rahe hain, aur method ke marks isi se milte hain. Bina wajah bataye seedha factor bana dena adhoora jawab lagta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Hamesha pehle substitution try karein. Agar koi number mil jaye, wohi limit hai.
2. Agar \(\frac{0}{0}\) mile, to limit abhi maloom nahin hui: pehle function simplify karein.
3. Factorize karein, common factor cancel karein (yeh zero nahin hota kyun ke \(x \ne a\)), phir number rakhein.
4. \(\frac{0}{0}\) wala factor hamesha \((x - a)\) hota hai jab \(x \to a\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\frac{0}{0} = 0\) ya \(\frac{0}{0} = 1\) likh kar ruk jana. \(\frac{0}{0}\) ki koi value nahin; yeh sirf ishara hai ke simplify karo.
2. Aisa factor cancel kar dena jo numerator aur denominator dono mein common na ho. Misaal: \(\frac{x+2}{x}\) mein \(x\) cancel nahin hota, kyun ke upar \(x\) poori expression ka factor nahin hai.
3. Beech ki lines mein "Lim" likhna bhool jana. Jab tak aap waqai \(x = a\) nahin rakhte, har line mein \(\lim_{x\to a}\) likhte rahein; warna equation ghalat ban jati hai.
